reviews.comment: All he does is read off of the PowerPoint slides verbatim. Homeworks and labs are easy, but the quizzes are incredibly difficult for no reason whatsoever. I found the midterm easier than the first quiz. You will survive this class even if you have 0 coding background, just be prepared to teach yourself a lot.

Zero people got an A in the class. Makes tests and quizzes unnecessarily hard for an introductory coding class. Average on the final was a 55. As far as i know, he's the only option for this class. Good luck.

For beginners, this is a very difficult course. However, if you are a smart and logical student, you will find it very interesting. The professor explains even the most complex concepts in a mathematical way. Students should not blame their teachers for their two brain cells not being able to connect properly in the class.

He just reads the slides and doesnt explain anything. The quizzes are just a bunch of trick questions that you wont understand because it's not like anything he has gone over in class (the averages were in the low 50's), and the midterm and final are 30% of your grade each. The ONLY reason i was able to get a B was cause of prior python knowledge.

Do NOT take this class. His low rating is well‑deserved. He discourages questions and makes you feel dumb whenever you ask for clarification. If you're new to programming, this course will be unnecessarily harsh and unsupportive, lookout for better-rated professors. Trust the RMP score, this is the last time I ignore it.

ask your TA any questions you have unless you want Yum to belittle you in front of the entire class. He's so rude and takes pride in the number of students that fail/drop his course. Don't waste $60 on his "mandatory" textbook; you're never gonna use it. You'll need to memorize every single bullet point on his slides to do well on the quizzes.

Listen, straight up, I did not take this class, but I listened to a couple of this guy's lectures, and he is the worst lecturer I have ever seen by far, super disrespectful to students asking questions, just a hateful guy that has no empathy for students trying to get through an introductory python course, and takes pride in his students' failure.
He is the worst teacher that I have ever taken in my life. On the tests and quizzes that averages are failing as he tries to trip you up. I would avoid at all costs.
This professor is a very tough grader and the lecture barely makes sense. Passing is a struggle and he doesn't seem to care about any of his students and if they pass or fail.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He won't tell you what will be on the exam or the quizzes and it's your ENTIRE grade! He writes his own exams and quizzes so good luck finding ANYTHING useful online. He doesn't like questions and will talk to you like the dumbest person on the planet if you dare ask one. He is a hateful person, and it shows. His mother didn't love him as a child.

He's bad, but often the only option. HW/Labs often have YT videos or are on LeetCode, so you can find similar to help on labs/HWs (each worth 10%). Use your time to study on impossible quizzes (20%) & MQ exams (60%). You don't need the required textbook; it may help, but he posts everything in the slides. Personally, it was a waste of $64.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most memorable part of his class was when he started trauma-dumping about how his kids never got him anything for Father's Day. Once you take his class, you'll understand why. He's a super hilarious guy, so he's fittingly comedically bad at his job too.

The most socially clueless teacher I have ever had. Was nearly impossible to approach for help, and would belittle and punish students for things entirely out of their control like lockdown browser issues. He was extremely hard to understand, with a heavy accent and fast speaking. He “teaches” by mindlessly reading dull slides. Useless teacher.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will question your God
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not teach the logic of coding and, even when he does, it is very difficult to follow because it is built upon other unexplained topics. This is an impossible class if you do not have lots of prior experience and do not want to be extremely reliant on outside resources. Lots of reading, lots of long HWs, and lots of long labs.

I hadn't ever seen a professor send students out of the classroom until him. He did them a favor. By far the most condescending and rude professor I've had.

He's also just unclear of what he expects for his quizzes. You'll put too much time/effort into studying just to get a 60. Isn't easy, even with experience. 

Don't be like me, believe RMP.
Don't do it. You don't deserve this. You're just a girl. And what's a girl to do when there's evil like this? A girlie's gotta go.

Despite taking ENGR 102, CSCE 110 is very tough, mainly due to the professor. Quizzes are 20% of the course grade, but average in the low 60s and contain niche problems that would never come up when coding. Labs and HW are free 100's but are only worth 20% combined. Exams are doable, but very little review/help is given beforehand. DO NOT TAKE!
Straight up he's a villain.

Yum is interesting professor. He does not teach, answer questions, or communicate anything, yet requires expertise from an introductory class. This is my third year and I've never met a professor so committed to belittling students and providing the least amount of resources for success while simultaneously expecting the upmost respect.

He is bad, boring, and does absolutely nothing to help his students. His quizzes are impossible without both advanced prior knowledge and complete memorization of his slides. We're 4/5 quizzes in and the mean has yet to be above a 60. Unsure which semester it started, but after Fall 2023 he increased the weight of his quizzes from 10% to 20%. Avoid

Yum is a questionable professor. He makes labs and homework pretty easy but quizzes impossible and exams very difficult. His lectures are mind numbingly boring, but you have to go because he takes an attendance grade. His class is equivalent to a grammar class for python. You could be an experienced coder and still do poorly in his class.

Hilariously bad at his job. Lectures are nonsensical, he often makes mistakes or isn't clear. Homework and 'Labs' are usually a free 100 if you know how to code. But the tests and quizzes will have niche questions that I'm sure even he couldn't answer on the spot, feels like gambling even with 3 years of python experience. Have an IDE in your head!

Funny at times, but mostly just reading off the slides (thick accent). The labs and exams are hard, but fair. The quizzes are hard and unfair, as several of the questions are based off of you having memorized specific slides. 

Good luck.

He is so very unclear on what he wants for all of the homework and labs. I get second hand embarrassment during his lectures when he tries and fails to run code from his terribly written slides on his machine and flounders trying to figure out why it didn't work. Also, he speaks in a way that is hard for me and other students to understand. AVOID!!
I dont think he's suited to be a professor, labs/homework wasn't bad, quizzes/tests were hard

My main complaint is that tests and quizzes cover really niche things that you wouldn't really see in code IRL or use. Labs and homeworks were fairly easy and TAs are helpful. Yum is not a good lecturer and pretty condescending so watch youtube videos and use zybooks
He was strict and impersonal. Its hard to get an A even if you know how to code.

Incredibly hard to understand lectures, and when you try to ask for help all he says is "ask your TA". Tests are based on your ability to memorize code, and can be incredibly challenging. Do not expect him to curve or round your grade up either.
Not a great lecturer due to a bit of an accent, but sufficeint enough.

If you have ZERO python experience don't take this class, otherwise use help from TA's, tutors, or online lectures. Look, this guy is a super sweet man and is really only strict on quiz or exam days, but his accent is so thick, and when you ask for help he says "idk ask your TA". Exams and quizzes are in person, online, and HARD (personally).

Gives about 1 whole lab assignments worth of EC. Quizzes and exams have super low averages, and are representative of how much you can memorize code fcns beforehand. Exams are mc and instantly graded, but quizzes and labs graded by TAs. quizzes are full of little gotcha questions, so read slides thoroughly and do hws in lecture/read slides on own.

Professor Yum expects you to know answers to questions that he's asking on the topic that he's teaching before even teaching it. This sometimes makes his lectures very confusing and hard to pay full attention to. Furthermore, the quizzes are not free bees by any means as the quiz average was in the 60% as 15% of your total grade.

I think he's a nice guy, but he isn't a good teacher. He often has to google questions that are asked of him during lecture. If many people aren't present when he walks into the room, he decides to take attendance that day. I only did well in this class because of prior knowledge. Please use any other option if this will be your first time coding.

By far the WORST professor I've ever taken. He's rude and derogatory, he will literally smile as he fails you. He was proud of how low the averages for his quizzes were. Make friends if you do get stuck in this class, it helps to talk about the material and trauma bond. So bad, I want to give it a zero, but that's not possible… so I give it a one.

He is probably the worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't even know how to complete the lab assignment. He said, “I don't know how to solve this problem; you should ask your TA.” He takes attendance every week and makes fun of you if you don't know how to respond to his questions. Please avoid taking his class if you can!

He was very challenging and a really tough grader. We had a quiz about every week and I do not think anyone ever got a 100 on them. I came in to class very knowledgeable about programming, yet I still failed every quiz.

His lectures and labs don't line up so often you will be doing assignments about stuff that you have not learned yet. If you have a question to ask him don't even bother, he will just ridicule you and tell you to ask TA because he doesn't know it. Takes attendance on days that students would usually miss. Overall he's a bad professor and very rude.

The exam is hard, and there is tons of homework. If you have never learned Python before, don't take his class; his lecture will become your nightmare. The lecture itself maybe 50% helpful for your homework and lab assignments, but the difficulty level of the lab assignments is about 80%, and the lecture is absolutely tedious. You have to trust RMP

Very test heavy with tests that do not test if you can code, but rather if you can memorize the content of the slides. Labs and TA's are very helpful, but the teacher himself does not grade you on coding ability.
this man is not doing enough to teach the material

Degrading to students and bad at teaching. Never hated a professor more than this guy. Quizzes average in the 60s, and he sporadically takes attendance, usually on bad weather days or right before breaks. It's a survivable course, if you don't know any coding, get the book and learn from that! His lectures are awful too.

I don't think I have despised a professor more. He was so degrading. I never missed a class, did all of the assignments, and barely made it out with a B. If it weren't for the quizzes and exams, I would've made a high A. Exam averages were in the 50/60's... Also, I didn't like the TA's. I had to figure the whole class out by myself. DON'T TAKE!!!

This man should not be a professor. He is full of himself and laughs when you ask a question. He gets a kick out of humiliating his students while reading black and white slides. Waited till the last possible minute to grade assignments so I never knew what my grade was in the class. SO MUCH HOMEWORK. Literally please take ANYONE else.

His lectures were barely understandable. Doesn't seem like he actually knows how to use technology very well. Wish there was another option for him. I ended up liking python but I learned it in spite of the professor not because of the professor. Get ready to teach your self python

Yum doesn't teach in an engaging way whatsoever. He takes attendance on Fridays before breaks and days it is stormy, when lots of people are not in class. I got a B by googling everything to try to learn it because his lectures didn't teach me at all. My midterm and exam were in the 50s range, but I passed because of quizzes & homework assignments.

Dude is objectively mean to students, and not in some joking way. Wholeheartedly I believe this man shouldn't be an instructor. Course wise not bad, though if you have no prior coding experience the lack of test reviews sucks. He just reads slides without any extrapolation or attempt to "teach" it and insults kids on the daily. Weird guy.

One of the rudest and most uncaring teachers I've ever seen. Frequently goes out of his way to insult or demean students for asking questions. Gives poor and confusing lectures while assigning homework far advanced of what he is teaching. Brags about having low averages and people failing his course. Do not take, especially without prior experience

Labs saved my grade. Quizzes are insanely hard & harshly graded. Final avg was a 60 last year. He takes attendance on random days that are worth 5% of grade (mostly on Fridays and before important stuff). He is not understanding of technical issues in class and will not answer questions during quizzes or exams. He made this class hard. Go to lab!!!

His lectures were really boring, black and white slides are NOT a good way to teach programming. Tests were on Canvas with online proctoring, he doesn't let you go back on questions and no scratch paper is allowed.

This class as a whole should have been simple and exciting to learn coding as someone who has not coded before. Like it is an intro level class right??? WRONG!!! This professor made this class a living nightmare!! He just goes over the slides in class, like I can do that myself.. He is also very rude and judgy towards his students. Do not take him.

If you have the option to never interact with Ki Hwan Yum in your life, I am envious of you. This man barely speaks English but is fluent in meaniehead (I can't use profanity or derogatory terms). He will go out of his way to make his students' life miserable. I wish Ki Hwan Yum nothing but the worst.

I felt like the only reason I got an A was because I had knowledge of python before taking this class. For an introductory class, this is a much more challenging way to be introduced to programming. Attendance is taken for a grade, but honestly just sneak out and review the lecture slides at home. He adds a few things in lectures, but not too much.

This is supposed to be an introductory CSCE class but this prof' exams are made for people who don't shower and sit behind their computer all day. Programming assignments and HW easy, quiz and exam average around the 60. Nobody showed up to class because it was useless.

All preparation material for final was a review sheet with 8 questions ;(

If you can take this class with someone else, DO IT. He is the type of professor that look down on students and enjoys blasting you in front of the class. You got an legit issue? Better drop the class since he has zero empathy and will not work with you. He claps to get peoples attention and its annoying to say the least.

Stupid attendance policy, calls you out for leaving early. Can't fathom that his 100-level course doesn't need to be taken as seriously as a doctorate program. Claps his hands to get your attention which gets incredibly irritating after a couple weeks. Literally only took his class for the credit because all the material was covered in ENGR102.

Yum really does not care about his students succeeding. If you ask a question, he will treat you like you are stupid. Class is 10% quizzes, 5% attendance, 30% labs, 20% homework, 15% midterm and 20% final. Does not offer any credit or replace any of the grades. He takes attendance 10 times per semester, usually fridays, before break and raining.

This prof is very strict. He will not round up your 89. He will call you out if you walk out of class. He will take attendance for a grade when there are no kids in class (usually before breaks or on Fridays). He doesn't seem like he wants to see his students succeed. However he will give points for the midterm and final if the avg is bad.

I honestly do not know how someone could give Dr. Yum a good review. Dr. Yum is easily one of the worst professors I have ever taken throughout my college career. His lectures are unorganized and leave students more confused than when they originally arrived. Grading is extremely harsh and quizzes are overly hard. Avoid at all costs.

Great professor. He takes attendance 10 times for 10% of the grade but if you attend class like you're supposed to, it's easy 10%. Quizzes are graded a harshly with little to no partial credit but the labs are easy with great TAs and homeworks are rather straightforward. There is a clear grading criteria so make sure you follow the format exactly.

110 is hard if without coding experience. Yum takes attendance when numbers are low. Uneventful lectures, so I mainly worked on labs and homework. Tests + quizzes are hard, so aim for high grades on labs and homework. Labs progress at faster rate than lecture, & the TA + PT were the reason why I had 100s on labs. Go to class/lab & you'll be good.

This class is just dumb. The labs do not align at all with the lectures, the quizzes are so much harder than anything else in the class, with averages in the 50's. There are many little things he does that annoy me such as clapping randomly in class and telling students to move to different seats. He is very old school. Never wanna see him again

His lectures were pretty useless and you would have to teach yourself if you were confused. If you have prior Python or coding experience, this class will be easy, but if not you will struggle. Takes attendance on days when students typically don't show up (Fridays, the Monday before thanksgiving, etc.) which was annoying.
Only annoying thing is when he claps his hands randomly. Other than that, his quizzes are the only hard grade in the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you're a student that is willing to try to learn then this class is easy. He takes attendance 10 times a semester, usually on Fridays or when it is raining, but if you just go to class like you are supposed to this is an easy 10% of your grade. Overall this experience was much better than ENGR 102 which was a nightmare for me.

I know the CSCE dept at A&M is trash, but this guy is the absolute bottom of the bin. He made a 100-level course harder than the 400 level classes that I am taking. He thinks it's funny to give out 0s on quizzes and he intentionally takes attendance on Fridays, days before holiday breaks, and days where students normally don't come to class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Most horrible professor at Texas A&M avoid at all cost. He will habitually have pop quizzes right before holidays and grade extremely harshly on projects
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The lectures were boring. He read black & white PowerPoints & did some code. There were 5 "homework" assignments (20%), 5 FR quizzes (10%), 9 labs (30%), a MC midterm (15%), & a MC final (20%). Takes attendance 10 times throughout the semester (5%). Everything was pretty easy, except quizzes (were short, 2 ?s, & graded w/little partial credit).
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont take Dr Yum. Lectures are unorganized and hes an ornery person. HW and labs are easy, but 0s on quizzes are common. On tests you cant go back on questions, and you arent allowed to write things down because its too easy. Only test advice was to pray. Got a 76 and 84 on midterm and final, he wouldnt budge on rounding my 79 up to a B
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This dude is not good. I know how to code and am struggling to keep a B in the class. I am typing this while waiting for my final and am not happy. Don't take this guy for the love of all things holy.

Yum is a good professor. He is very nice, caring and willing to work with you if you just ask him for help. He is sometimes hard to understand because of his accent, but you get used to it. I took this class online, so I kind of had to teach myself a lot of the material, but his lectures were still helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Yum is funny and knows his stuff. Quizzes and exams try to trick you, so be careful. First half will be easy if you have any coding experience. Labs/HW are easy, takes attendance at 10 random times, mostly on fridays/when it rains Only complaint is that he could be a bit more understanding when students have issues at home and miss assignments

If you've never taken programming in your life. DO NOT TAKE THIS. I had never done programming and this was the hardest class ever. His lectures did not make sense to me nor could I understand him. The labs assigned were long and hard. He only takes attendance on Fridays and days that rain or are likely to skip.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a tough grader and was constantly trying to trick you on quizzes and tests, but that made you really understand what was going on. Although the quiz grades are low, it doesn't make up a lot of your average. Gives tests back quickly, and curves so the average is an 80. Go to class- he takes attendance on rainy days and Fridays particularly.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Constantly spoke in class about how he wanted people to drop the course because they were going to fail. Gloated about quiz averages being 10/50 and laughed when people asked for a curve. He might know the subject but he does not know how to teach. He doesn't grade anything himself and it takes 3-4 weeks for grades
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Yum is a really funny guy, and he is very educated about the subject. He will explain concepts that he will tell you will not be tested on, but he cares about the students actually learning it. His tests are hard because he tries to trick you, but if you study hard you should be fine.

Was super responsive through email and very kind. I read textbooks or looked up parts I didn't understand and found the class fairly easy. A textbook isn't required for the assignments but I would recommend that you use an online one so you can clarify confusing parts.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you've taken a computer science class before you'll be fine. Lectures are hard to understand, you're better off learning everything on YouTube. You can fail quizzes/midterm/final and still get a B. Use Chegg for all labs and homework. He takes attendance, but I skipped a ton and still got an 8/10 for it.
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader on the quizzes but the class isn't too bad. You have a homework and a programming assignment every other week that you can usually use the internet to help. I never went to the labs and went to class about half of the time. Attendance isn't mandatory but he will take it 5-10 times. A good guy and can be funny on occasion.

I managed to fail every quiz (except he last one where i got an 80), got a 67 on midterm and 71 on the final. Got a mixture of As and Bs on my homework and mainly As in my labs. Missed two lectures (he take attendance on Fridays). I ended the class with a B!! Hes a touch grader on quizzes but dont let that scare you! Chegg it for HW and quiz

Dr. Yum does not care much about the lecture. He takes attendance once in a while. There are 2 midterms, he reads from the slides and you only get to practice in lab. It is not a terrible Class if you are committed to get a good grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: He is usually a fair grader, but the class itself was not helpful. He has a very heavy accent that makes it hard to understand him, and he usually didn't understand questions we asked him. Attendance is mandatory. The class starts out really easy, but gets really hard by the end, so make sure you put in the time and effort required.
Overall, he's fair. This class was split between homework and lab work, with a final that was pretty much just what was on the homework. He won't ever be my favorite prof, but he's not bad to take.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Yum's lectures are hard to follow at times, and his accent doesn't help. His exams were very easy and based on the textbook (which was only $10 to buy). The homework and lab assignments started off very easy but got extremely difficult by the end of the class. If you can focus and spend a good amount of time on the assignments, you can get an A
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Yum was a pretty good professor. He was not exceptional or enlightened me in some dramatic way but he was funny and covered every topic he expected you to know in depth. I think his lectures are a bit hard to focus on at times. He's an understanding professor who is willing to work with you if you mess and he cares about the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria
